newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France allowed to buy Boeings, Airbus -source.
newsitem.headline: Air France allowed to buy Boeings, Airbus -source.

text.p: The French government has cleared the way for state-owned Air France to buy Boeing and Airbus passenger jets when airline board members meet on Wednesday to decide on its fleet acquisition, an official source told Reuters on Tuesday.
"We are inclined to a balanced solution between Airbus and Boeing," said the source on Tuesday, speaking on condition of anonymity. "There should an agreement tomorrow."

A committee of the Air France board is expected on Wednesday to recommend purchase of 10 Airbus A340-300 and 10 Boeing 777-200 jets for its long-range fleet, business newspaper Les Echos reported on Tuesday.

Transport minister Bernard Pons has been pushing airline chairman Christian Blanc into buying exclusively from French-based Airbus Industrie, rather than mixing the purchase with archrival Boeing, industry and union sources have said.

Apart from the symbolic value of the French flag carrier, which has received 20 billion francs in state funds, buying from a U.S. company, the Boeing 777 and Airbus 340 are considered by some in the aerospace industry to be competing products.
Two other sources close to the talks said the split purchase was expected to be approved.
